newsitem.title: FRANCE: France calls for coalition in Kabul.
newsitem.headline: France calls for coalition in Kabul.

text.p: France called on Friday for an end to civil strife in Afganistan and the creation of a coalition government in Kabul.

"France renews its call for a cease-fire and a dialogue in light of the need for national reconciliation and the creation of a government representative of all parties," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.

He said France also wished to recall its attachment to human rights "and particularly to the condition of women" in light of the imposition of strict Islamic law by the Taleban administration which took power in Kabul two weeks ago.
Measures ordering women not to work or leave their homes unless accompanied by male members of their families have been severely criticised by the French media and human rights groups.
The situation in Afghanistan looked precarious on Friday as Taleban militiamen faced guerrilla attacks near the Afghan capital and the prospect of a military alliance among its foes in the north.
